correctness.rationale: For a perfect graph, the inspected full-text facet theorem gives the complete irredundant inequalities \(-1\le 2x(C)-t\le1\) for every clique \(C\). Their normals have exact Euclidean norm \(\sqrt{4|C|+1}\). Opposite facets of the centrally symmetric polytope force every inscribed ball radius to be at most the reciprocal of each such norm, and the centered ball at the maximum-clique bound satisfies all facets. The exact vertex set consists of antipodal vectors \(\pm(\chi_S,1)\), whose squared norms are \(|S|+1\); the maximum stable set gives both a containing centered sphere and an antipodal diameter lower bound. The unique-circumcenter argument follows by adding the two squared-distance inequalities for a maximum antipodal pair. All quantifiers and normalization choices are explicit.

value.rationale: The result assigns two basic Euclidean invariants of a natural centrally symmetric polytope family exactly to two central graph invariants: the clique number and the stability number. It also identifies the precise inner and outer contact structures. This is a structural metric theorem for the whole perfect-graph Hansen family, not a finite table, parameter substitution, or isolated numerical calculation. The formulas let either graph invariant be recovered directly from a canonical Euclidean radius.
